messages:
maria_ops: FYI I'm seeing sustained packet loss spikes from nodes in az-2c since ~1934567800, GPU p95 tail latency up and a bunch of 502s from the runtime.

deploy-bot: [ALERT] network.metrics.packet_loss > 5% in cluster-ggp-prod az-2c (triggered at 1934567815) :warning:

jonah_infra: Confirming. I can see intermittent 30-70% packet loss on the host eth0 for a subset of hosts (10/120). Kernel counters show tx_retries ballooning.

maria_ops: Can we soft-drain the affected nodes so model-serving pods fail over to the rest of the fleet? Prefer graceful so KV caches warm elsewhere.

jonah_infra: Plan: 1) annotate hosts with "soft-drain=true" 2) adjust routing weight for az-2c in the traffic router -> reduce to 20% 3) cordon & evict GPU pods with --grace-period=120 4) monitor cold starts and cost delta.

sara_sre: +1. Add a temp autoscale bump for pod replicas for the affected deployments (chat, generation) while we shift traffic. I'll watch latency SLOs.

kevin_net: Reached out to cloud provider support, they reported a fiber repair ticket for that PoP, ETA 2-3h. For now we should avoid aggressive cross-AZ egress that might amplify packet loss.

ops-oncall: tagging runbook link: <https://internal/runbooks/az-degradation|az-deg runbook> — step 2 has draining guidance.

jonah_infra: K8s commands I'm running (will paste):
```bash
kubectl get nodes -l az=az-2c -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl label {} infra/soft-drain=true --overwrite
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l az=az-2c -o name); do kubectl cordon $n; done
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120 --force
```

maria_ops: When you reduce router weight, please reduce at the ingress edge first (api-gateway) then backend LB. We want to avoid in-flight request failovers.

jonah_infra: Roger. Reducing router weight now: api-gw az2c -> 25% (was 60%). backend-routes -> 20%.

deploy-bot: [INFO] router.update applied by jonah_infra at 1934567920; api-gw weights: {az-2a:40, az-2b:35, az-2c:25}

kevin_net: I've added temporary BGP prepends on our transit to prefer other AZs for new flows. Old flows may still hit az-2c until TCP timeout.

maria_ops: How many GPU pods moved? Are we seeing OOM/cold-start errors?

jonah_infra: ~85 pods evicted so far, most came up in other AZs. Seeing a spike in prometheus scrape latency and a handful of 503s from model-serving due to warmup. Past minute p95 token latency +120ms. No OOMs.

sara_sre: Rolling autoscale applied (+20% on generation workers). Monitoring quality and cost. Forecast: small cost bump for extra replicas ~+6%/hr.

ops-oncall: Provider ETA still 2-3h. Are we comfortable keeping az-2c at 20% weight and soft-draining the rest?

maria_ops: Yes — keep soft-drain label so the scheduler avoids packing new long-lived KV-cache pods there. If provider ETA slips beyond 3h, we'll shift to full drain.

jonah_infra: Added a temporary placement rule: avoid scheduling pods with label role=kv-cache to az=az-2c.

kevin_net: Quick note: customers in region eu-west-2 may see slightly higher latencies; we're routing more traffic to az-2a/2b. Sending status update to status.redwood.ai now.

maria_ops: Thanks. I'll keep watching logs for retransmits and the kernel counters. If packet loss drops below 1% for 10m, we'll reverse weights gradually.

deploy-bot: [NOTE] incident-channel created: #incident-1934567890-az2c.

jonah_infra: Current metrics snapshot: packet_loss az-2c = 18% -> after edge weight change observed effective 7% for new flows. p95 token latency returned to +30ms over baseline.

maria_ops: Good. We'll maintain this posture and reconvene in 30m. If provider confirms fiber fix, plan is to lift soft-drain and revert weights slowly over 20m.
